title: Book Two · Chapter 161: The Cupboard Game
story:
On Sunday morning, Ronan makes a little plan of the kitchen. He puts a small square for the cupboard and a long square for the table. Then he writes a note for Dad.

The note sends him to the cupboard for a cup. After that, he must go to the table for a spoon.

Dad reads it with great care. He walks to the cupboard, opens the door, and brings back a bowl.

“Wrong thing,” Ronan says.

“It can hold tea.”

“The note says a cup.”

Dad gets the cup. He takes it to the table, puts it on his head, and waits.

Ronan laughs. “That part is not on the note.”

“Then your note needs more words.”

Mum watches from the door. “The cup needs a different table.”

Dad puts it down before it falls. He takes a spoon and brings both things to Ronan. Ronan gives him a small paper star.

“For your fine work.”

“Does it come with breakfast?”

“Only if you read the next page.”

They eat first. Then Ronan takes out a new room plan. Miss Wu gave him this page to use at home. It is for home use and cannot count toward the six results.

This time, the collection desk is beside the garden door. A separate note changes the waiting place during rain. Ronan puts one finger on each note. First he reads where people usually wait. Then he reads the change.

Dad washes the plates while Ronan works. No one points to the answer.

After ten minutes, Ronan asks Mum to use the question card. She sits opposite him and reads the first question exactly as it appears.

“Where do I collect the packet?”

“At the desk beside the garden door.”

“It is raining. Does the desk move?”

“No. You wait inside by the tall window. Then you go to the same desk.”

He shows her both lines. She turns over the question card. The answers on the back match his explanation.

“You have it,” she says.

Ronan breathes out and smiles. He writes HOME at the top of the page. He wants to put a bright mark beside it, but his coloured pencil is at school. An ordinary pencil makes a clear enough mark.

Dad comes back and looks over his shoulder.

“Can I get my star now?” Ronan asks.

Dad takes the paper star from his own pocket. It has a soft corner and a little water mark.

“Used, but still good.”

Ronan takes it. He puts it beside the home page. He keeps both apart from the six school practice papers. Mum needs the table for her cloth. Ronan carries the whole small game to his room.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

cupboard＝碗柜；separate＝单独的；toward＝计入、朝向；match＝与……相符。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan这次怎样独立读懂两个地点安排？
2. 这张家庭练习纸为什么不能增加选拔记录？

## 读句子

**An ordinary pencil makes a clear enough mark.**

拆开看：An ordinary pencil / makes / a clear enough mark.

一支普通铅笔／就能画出／足够清楚的记号。
